entries.title: PRNG
entries.summaryMd: A pseudorandom number generator (PRNG), also known as a deterministic random bit generator (DRBG), is an algorithm for generating a sequence of numbers whose properties approximate the properties of sequences of random numbers. The PRNG-generated sequence is not truly random, because it is completely determined by an initial value, called the PRNG's seed (which may include truly random values). Although sequences that are closer to truly random can be generated using hardware random number generators, pseudorandom number generators are important in practice for their speed in number generation and their reproducibility.

Spoofed packets are commonly used to carry out denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, exploit network and system vulnerabilities, and gain unauthorized access to corporate networks and data.

A state in which information has remained unaltered from the point it was produced by a source, during transmission, storage, and eventual receipt by the destination.

entries.title: intent
entries.summaryMd: A state of mind or desire to achieve an objective.

senses.definitionMd: A state of mind or desire to achieve an objective.

citation.citationText: NICCS Cybersecurity Vocabulary, "machine learning and evolution"

entries.summaryMd: A small application program that is automatically downloaded and executed and that performs an unauthorized function on an information system.

senses.definitionMd: A small application program that is automatically downloaded and executed and that performs an unauthorized function on an information system.

entries.summaryMd: Program code intended to perform an unauthorized function or process that will have adverse impact on the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of an information system.

senses.definitionMd:
Program code intended to perform an unauthorized function or process that will have adverse impact on the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of an information system.

Includes software, firmware, and scripts.

entries.title: malicious logic
entries.summaryMd: Hardware, firmware, or software that is intentionally included or inserted in a system to perform an unauthorized function or process that will have adverse impact on the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Hardware, firmware, or software that is intentionally included or inserted in a system to perform an unauthorized function or process that will have adverse impact on the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of an information system.

entries.title: Malvertising

senses.definitionMd: a malicious attack that involves injecting harmful code into legitimate online advertising networks

entries.title: malware

senses.definitionMd: Software that compromises the operation of a system by performing an unauthorized function or process.

Implementing appropriate risk-reduction controls based on risk management priorities and analysis of alternatives.

entries.title: moving target defense
entries.summaryMd: The presentation of a dynamic attack surface, increasing an adversary's work factor necessary to probe, attack, or maintain presence in a cyber target.

senses.definitionMd: The presentation of a dynamic attack surface, increasing an adversary's work factor necessary to probe, attack, or maintain presence in a cyber target.

entries.title: network resilience
entries.summaryMd: The ability of a network to: (1) provide continuous operation (i.e., highly resistant to disruption and able to operate in a degraded mode if damaged); (2) recover effectively if failure does occur; and (3) scale to meet rapid or unpredictable demands.

senses.definitionMd: The ability of a network to: (1) provide continuous operation (i.e., highly resistant to disruption and able to operate in a degraded mode if damaged); (2) recover effectively if failure does occur; and (3) scale to meet rapid or unpredictable demands.

senses.definitionMd: The emerging field that studies how the brain relates to performance in everyday settings and at work, integrating neuroscience and ergonomics to design safer and more efficient systems and understand brain-performance relationships.

entries.title: Neuromorphic

senses.definitionMd: Neuromorphic computing is a method of computing that uses artificial neurons to mimic the human brain's structure and function. The word "neuromorphic" means "characteristic of the shape of the brain or neurons"

entries.summaryMd: a malicious technique where an attacker gains control over a target's proxy server, allowing them to intercept and manipulate the targets internet traffic

entries.title: Pseudorandom Number Generator
entries.summaryMd: A pseudorandom number generator (PRNG), also known as a deterministic random bit generator (DRBG), is an algorithm for generating a sequence of numbers whose properties approximate the properties of sequences of random numbers. The PRNG-generated sequence is not truly random, because it is completely determined by an initial value, called the PRNG's seed (which may include truly random values). Although sequences that are closer to truly random can be generated using hardware random number generators, pseudorandom number generators are important in practice for their speed in number generation and their reproducibility.

senses.definitionMd: A pseudorandom number generator (PRNG), also known as a deterministic random bit generator (DRBG), is an algorithm for generating a sequence of numbers whose properties approximate the properties of sequences of random numbers. The PRNG-generated sequence is not truly random, because it is completely determined by an initial value, called the PRNG's seed (which may include truly random values). Although sequences that are closer to truly random can be generated using hardware random number generators, pseudorandom number generators are important in practice for their speed in number generation and their reproducibility.

entries.title: public key
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic key that may be widely published and is used to enable the operation of an asymmetric (public key) cryptographic algorithm.

senses.definitionMd:
A cryptographic key that may be widely published and is used to enable the operation of an asymmetric (public key) cryptographic algorithm.

The public part of an asymmetric key pair that is uniquely associated with an entity and that may be made public.

entries.title: public key cryptography
entries.summaryMd: A branch of cryptography in which a cryptographic system or algorithms use two uniquely linked keys: a public key and a private key (a key pair).

senses.definitionMd: A branch of cryptography in which a cryptographic system or algorithms use two uniquely linked keys: a public key and a private key (a key pair).

entries.title: public key infrastructure
entries.summaryMd: A framework consisting of standards and services to enable secure, encrypted communication and authentication over potentially insecure networks such as the Internet.

senses.definitionMd:
A framework consisting of standards and services to enable secure, encrypted communication and authentication over potentially insecure networks such as the Internet.

A framework and services for generating, producing, distributing, controlling, accounting for, and revoking (destroying) public key certificates.

entries.title: Quantum Random Number Generator
entries.summaryMd: A Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) is a device that produces truly random numbers by measuring unpredictable quantum mechanical processes, such as photon arrival times or vacuum fluctuations, rather than using algorithms. Unlike pseudo-random generators, QRNGs provide foundational, non-deterministic security for cryptography, IoT devices, and simulations, ensuring keys are fundamentally unpredictable.

senses.definitionMd: A Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) is a device that produces truly random numbers by measuring unpredictable quantum mechanical processes, such as photon arrival times or vacuum fluctuations, rather than using algorithms. Unlike pseudo-random generators, QRNGs provide foundational, non-deterministic security for cryptography, IoT devices, and simulations, ensuring keys are fundamentally unpredictable.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to adapt to changing conditions and prepare for, withstand, and rapidly recover from disruption.

entries.title: response

The activities that address the short-term, direct effects of an incident and may also support short-term recovery.

In cybersecurity, response encompasses both automated and manual activities.

entries.summaryMd: The potential for an unwanted or adverse outcome resulting from an incident, event, or occurrence, as determined by the likelihood that a particular threat will exploit a particular vulnerability, with the associated consequences.

senses.definitionMd: The potential for an unwanted or adverse outcome resulting from an incident, event, or occurrence, as determined by the likelihood that a particular threat will exploit a particular vulnerability, with the associated consequences.

entries.title: risk analysis
entries.summaryMd: The systematic examination of the components and characteristics of risk.

senses.definitionMd: The systematic examination of the components and characteristics of risk.

entries.summaryMd: The product or process which collects information and assigns values to risks for the purpose of informing priorities, developing or comparing courses of action, and informing decision making.

senses.definitionMd:
The product or process which collects information and assigns values to risks for the purpose of informing priorities, developing or comparing courses of action, and informing decision making.

The appraisal of the risks facing an entity, asset, system, or network, organizational operations, individuals, geographic area, other organizations, or society, and includes determining the extent to which adverse circumstances or events could result in harmful consequences.

entries.title: risk-based data management
entries.summaryMd: A structured approach to managing risks to data and information by which an organization selects and applies appropriate security controls in compliance with policy and commensurate with the sensitivity and value of the data.

senses.definitionMd: A structured approach to managing risks to data and information by which an organization selects and applies appropriate security controls in compliance with policy and commensurate with the sensitivity and value of the data.

entries.title: risk management
entries.summaryMd: The process of identifying, analyzing, assessing, and communicating risk and accepting, avoiding, transferring or controlling it to an acceptable level considering associated costs and benefits of any actions taken.

senses.definitionMd:
The process of identifying, analyzing, assessing, and communicating risk and accepting, avoiding, transferring or controlling it to an acceptable level considering associated costs and benefits of any actions taken.

Includes: 1) conducting a risk assessment; 2) implementing strategies to mitigate risks; 3) continuous monitoring of risk over time; and 4) documenting the overall risk management program.

entries.summaryMd: A set of software tools with administrator-level access privileges installed on an information system and designed to hide the presence of the tools, maintain the access privileges, and conceal the activities conducted by the tools.

entries.title: secret key

A rule or set of rules that govern the acceptable use of an organization's information and services to a level of acceptable risk and the means for protecting the organization's information assets.
